newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch consider ban on pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: Dutch consider ban on pyramid schemes.

text.p: The Netherlands said on Wednesday it was considering banning pyramid investment schemes following the collapse of such schemes in other countries.
Finance Minister Gerrit Zalm said about 400 million guilders ($210 million) was invested in the estimated 60 pyramid investment schemes operating in the Netherlands.
He said these schemes had claimed victims in the Netherlands and he wanted to outlaw them but first the Dutch legislation had to be changed.
"For me it's important to do something about it. With the law we have now, we can't do much about it. We probably need a new law to forbid them," he told reporters.
Earlier this month, the Dutch central bank warned investors about the high risks of pyramid schemes, which rely on funds from new investors to pay high rates of interesting to existing investors.
The collapses of such schemes in Albania left thousands destitute and sparked an armed uprising against the government in the Balkan country.
Many people in Russia and Romania have also lost their savings in similar schemes.
